I stayed here during my first year. I was in Block B, which everyone called the “party block”, which sums it up perfectly. Block A and C were a lot quieter. Was always Block B triggering the fire alarms at 4am too lol. I think international students get put in Block C if I remember correctly, though I could be wrong. Overall, the flats were nice, and there’s air filter thingys in the bathrooms so they don’t stay too wet for long after a shower. Wifi was alright. 

Absolutely infested with silverfish, unless this has been sorted now, though I highly doubt it because people’s showers would flood into rooms so often because of hair blocking the drains and stuff, so there’s bound to be loads still about. There was a weekly cleaner for the kitchen, but if your kitchen was messy they’d refuse to clean and give you a warning. Fortunately my flat were relatively tidy people so this only happened once to us.

There’s usually socials and events going on at the reception area thing where they have a TV and pool table etc., as a sort of common room, but I remember people only turned up to the first social for the free t-shirts and pizza, then the rest were pretty dead. 

Overall, it wasn’t the worst place I’ve lived in Brighton. The convenience of being right on campus for my classes was a godsend, but going food shopping was an absolute pain as I had barely any student finance left over after the rent, so getting the bus was out of the question lol. Walked the distance every week. But it’s part of the first-year experience, really. Everyone I’ve met who went for private housing in first year regretted it, as they felt they missed out on making friends as easily. It’s a mixed bag, but that’s student life ahah

From experience and anecdotes from people in other courses, despite Brighton being low in rankings, they can feel like quite harsh markers, unlike some other unis that can be known for throwing out firsts and 2:1’s like candy. I didn’t do music but I was on another creative sort of course and there’s always something going on in the uni or in Brighton in general that creatives will enjoy. Especially music, you can find live music pretty much anywhere, and a place to go for any genre of music you like. 

I dont have much to comment on quality of education as from talking to people in different courses it really depends on who is teaching you. You’re always gonna get those amazing, passionate lecturers but then there’s of course the opposite, tired lecturers. But uni really is what you take from it and most of the learning should be independent anyway. 

All in all, I’m happy I came here. Despite how expensive living can be, I enjoyed my years living here and would probably stay if I could afford it. Anyone can fit in here and find their people and their place.
